summary: Same pattern beyond doubt — a hard-edged 20-px red/white/green block marquee stepping one block every ~2 s — but the port chases in the opposite direction, uses a purer green than the original's chartreuse, and omits the original's 2 s solid-red startup hold.
observations: Pairing is NOT a mismatch: both sides render the identical concept — a strip divided into fixed 20-pixel solid blocks cycling red / white / green, the whole assignment jumping one block every ~2 s. No cross-fades, no twinkle, no per-pixel noise on either side.

Exact colours (--dump, 60 px default rig, steady state): red is 255,0,0 on both; white is 114,114,114 on both; GREEN DIFFERS — original 51,255,0 (yellow-shifted chartreuse), port 0,255,0 (pure green). This is the whole reason the mean-red stat differs (orig meanR 140 vs port 123); meanG and meanB match at 123 / 38.

MOTION DIRECTION IS REVERSED. On a 300-px rig (5 spatial repeats, so direction is unambiguous) the original's block sequence goes [G,R,W] → [W,G,R] → [R,W,G]: content shifts +20 px (toward higher pixel index) each step. The port goes [W,G,R] → [G,R,W] → [R,W,G]: content shifts -20 px each step. Confirmed at t=3/5/7/9 s and again at t=201/203/205/207 s.

STARTUP TRANSIENT, original only: for the first 2.0 s the original holds the ENTIRE strip solid 255,0,0 (all 60 px, verified at t=0, 0.05, 0.5, 1.0, 1.9 s) and only begins the tri-colour marquee at t=2.0 s. The port shows the three-block arrangement from frame 0. This state never recurs on the original in 200 s of observation.

Step cadence matches almost exactly and is fps-invariant on both sides: at 5/10/20/40 fps the original's inter-change gap is exactly 2.0 s + 1 frame (2.20 / 2.10 / 2.05 / 2.025 s) while the port's is exactly 2.000 s at every rate. Both are time-based, not frame-stepped; the residual ~1-frame difference is a >= vs > boundary and is invisible.

Block size is a FIXED 20 pixels on both sides, not a fraction of the strip: at 12 px both render one solid colour, at 30 px both render 20+10, at 60 px both render 3 blocks, at 300 px both render 15 blocks with a 60-px spatial repeat. Identical scaling behaviour — no indexing divergence.
Both sides are fully deterministic: seed 1 and seed 1234 produce byte-identical arrangements and timings on each side.

Both sides are healthy in steady state — at --skip 200 both report brightnessTrend 'steady', meanBrightness 100 (orig) / 95 (port), and the same 2 s stepping. Neither freezes, decays, or saturates. High zeroMotionFrames (273/300 orig, 270/300 port in the 60 s survey) is correct for a pattern that holds a still image between block jumps, not a freeze.
Control surfaces match: both sides expose ZERO controls (probe run reports '(no settable controls)' for orig and port). Neither side has a missing or extra dial.
Neither side binds sensor globals (wantsSensors false on both), so the synthetic feed is irrelevant here.
feedback: Reverse the chase direction. The original advances the colour assignment toward HIGHER pixel indices each step (a block that is green at x=0..19 is green at x=20..39 two seconds later); the port advances toward lower indices. Everything else about the motion — step size (exactly one 20-px block) and dwell (~2 s) — is already correct, so this is purely the sign of the shift.
Change the green. The original's green is 51,255,0 (a chartreuse / yellow-shifted green); the port uses 0,255,0. Red (255,0,0) and white (114,114,114) are already exact matches — do not touch them.

Add the original's opening hold: the original lights the WHOLE strip solid red (255,0,0, every pixel) for the first 2.0 s of the run, then falls into the three-block marquee. The port starts in the marquee immediately. One-off transient, but it is 2 s of visibly different output at power-on.
Do not change the block size or the step cadence — both are already pixel-exact (fixed 20-px blocks regardless of strip length, 2.0 s per step, time-based rather than frame-coupled).
